elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement for convenience.
elements.evidence: The added standalone sentence expressly permits the Company to terminate the Agreement for convenience at any time.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause requires ninety (90) days' prior notice, not 30 days.

elements.element: Customer's termination-for-convenience notice must be written.
elements.evidence: The standalone right requires ninety (90) days' prior written notice.

elements.element: Upon Customer's termination for convenience, Customer receives a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees.
elements.evidence: No operative language requires any refund of prepaid fees. The absence of prepaid fees is not demonstrably established.

elements.element: Vendor may not terminate for convenience effective during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Section 4.1 provides that termination by HDI is effective only at the end of the then-current term.

elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement for convenience.
elements.evidence: The standalone sentence expressly permits the Company to terminate the Agreement for convenience at any time.

elements.element: Customer's termination-for-convenience notice period must be between 60 and 90 days.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause requires ninety (90) days' prior written notice, which is within the permitted 60–90 day range.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee payable by Customer must not exceed three months' fees.
elements.evidence: The Termination Payment is expressly capped at the amounts payable to HDI under Section 3.1 for the three months preceding the Termination Date.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate the Agreement for convenience.
elements.evidence: Section 4.1 permits either party, including HDI, to terminate on notice without requiring cause.

elements.element: Vendor's termination for convenience may be effective only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: The added proviso states that termination by HDI shall be effective only at the end of the then-current term.

elements.element: Vendor must provide 90 days' notice of termination for convenience.
elements.evidence: Section 4.1 requires either party, including HDI, to provide ninety (90) days' written notice.

result.reason: The operative language fully implements the fallback: Customer receives a 90-day convenience-termination right, the Termination Payment is capped at three months of Section 3.1 payments, and HDI may terminate only at term-end on 90 days' written notice. It does not satisfy the preferred position because Customer must give 90 rather than 30 days' notice and no pro-rata refund of prepaid fees is required. The changes are confined to the fallback requirements and do not alter unrelated commercial terms, although drafting quality is reduced by duplicative Customer termination language and the clause's pre-existing structural and grammatical defects.
